title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
kicker: Cambridge Primary Checkpoint · Mathematics 0096 · Stage 6 · Number
summary: Estimate, add and subtract fractions with different denominators using common denominators and equivalent fractions — with fraction-bar diagrams, worked examples and a Checkpoint-style quiz.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Estimate, add and subtract fractions with different denominators (6Nf.05)

blocks.text: You already know how to add fractions with the **same** denominator: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7. In Stage 6 you add and subtract fractions with **different** denominators, such as 1/2 + 1/3, and you estimate the answer first so you can check it.
Key words

items: denominator
المقام — tells you the size of the parts (halves, thirds, sixths…)
common denominator
مقام مشترك — a denominator that both fractions can be changed to
multiple
مضاعف — a number in the times table: multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16 …
lowest common multiple (LCM)
المضاعف المشترك الأصغر — the smallest number in both times tables (LCM of 4 and 6 is 12)
equivalent fraction
كسر مكافئ — same value, different numbers: 1/2 = 3/6
benchmark fractions
كسور مرجعية — easy fractions to compare with: 0, 1/2 and 1
estimate
تقدير — a quick, close answer to check your working
simplify
يبسّط — divide numerator and denominator by a common factor

blocks.text: 1. Why the denominators must be the same

You can only add or subtract parts that are the **same size**. A half and a third are different-sized pieces, so 1/2 + 1/3 is **not** 2/5. First cut both into pieces of the same size — sixths — then count them.

blocks.text: **Never add the denominators.** 1/3 + 1/4 is not 2/7: 2/7 is less than 1/3, and adding 1/4 must make the answer bigger than 1/3.
2. The method

items: **Estimate** the answer using 0, 1/2 and 1 (see section 3).
Find a **common denominator**: a number that both denominators divide into. The lowest common multiple (LCM) keeps the numbers small.
Change each fraction to an **equivalent fraction** with that denominator (multiply top and bottom by the same number).
Add or subtract the **numerators only**. Keep the denominator the same.
**Simplify** the answer, and change an improper fraction to a mixed number if needed. Compare with your estimate.

blocks.text: **Choosing the common denominator — three cases:**

rows: One denominator is a multiple of the other
The denominators have no common factor
LCM = 12 (4 × 6 = 24 also works, but you must simplify more)

blocks.text: 3. Estimating with 0, 1/2 and 1
Before calculating, decide whether each fraction is close to **0**, **1/2** or **1**. Compare the numerator with the denominator:

items: Numerator very small compared with the denominator → close to 0 (1/9, 1/10, 2/15).
Numerator about half of the denominator → close to 1/2 (3/8, 4/9, 5/11, 6/13).
Numerator nearly equal to the denominator → close to 1 (4/5, 7/8, 11/12).

blocks.text: **Using an estimate to check.** If you work out 3/8 + 4/5 and get 7/13, your estimate (about 1 1/2) tells you at once that something is wrong — 7/13 is about 1/2.
4. Word problems and mixed numbers
**"What fraction is left?"** The whole is 1 = the same number on top and bottom. Omar eats 1/3 of a cake and his sister eats 1/4. Together: 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12. Left: 12/12 − 7/12 = **5/12**.
**Mixed numbers.** Add or subtract the whole numbers and the fractions separately, or change to improper fractions:

items: 2 1/2 − 3/4: change to improper fractions: 5/2 − 3/4 = 10/4 − 3/4 = 7/4 = 1 3/4

blocks.title: القاعدة الذهبية
items: ممنوع تجمع أو تطرح المقامات! وحّد المقامات الأول، وبعدين اجمع أو اطرح البسط بس والمقام يفضل زي ما هو.
قبل ما تحل، قدّر: الكسر ده قريب من صفر ولا نص ولا واحد؟ وبعد ما تحل، قارن إجابتك بالتقدير.

blocks.text: Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Work out 2/5 + 1/3. [1 mark]

items: Estimate: 2/5 is a bit less than 1/2, 1/3 is between 0 and 1/2 → answer a bit less than 1.
5 and 3 have no common factor, so the common denominator is 15.
6/15 + 5/15 = **11/15**. It cannot be simplified, and it is a bit less than 1 ✓.

blocks.text: **Worked example 2** — Work out 5/6 − 3/8. [1 mark]

Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, **24**. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, **24**. LCM = 24. 5/6 = 20/24 and 3/8 = 9/24. 20/24 − 9/24 = **11/24**. **Common mistake:** writing 2/2 (subtracting top and bottom separately).
**Worked example 3** — Work out 3/4 + 2/3. Give your answer as a mixed number. [1 mark]
Common denominator 12: 9/12 + 8/12 = 17/12. 17 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 5, so the answer is **1 5/12**. Estimate: 1 + 1/2 = 1 1/2 — close ✓.
**Worked example 4** — Without working out the exact answer, ring the best estimate of 4/7 + 8/9:  1/2   1   1 1/2   2 [1 mark]
4/7 is close to 1/2 (4 is about half of 7) and 8/9 is close to 1. Estimate 1/2 + 1 = **1 1/2**. (Exact: 36/63 + 56/63 = 92/63 = 1 29/63, which is about 1.46 ✓.)
**Worked example 5** — Yara reads 1/4 of her book on Monday and 3/8 of it on Tuesday. What fraction of the book does she still have to read? [2 marks]

items: Fraction read: 1/4 + 3/8 = 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8 (1 method mark).
Whole book = 8/8. Still to read: 8/8 − 5/8 = **3/8**.

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** giving 5/8 as the final answer. Read the question again — it asks what is **left**.
**Worked example 6** — Leila says: "1/2 + 1/5 = 2/7." Explain how you know she is wrong, and write the correct answer. [2 marks]

**Answer:** 2/7 is less than 1/2 (half of 7 is 3.5, and 2 is less than 3.5), but adding 1/5 to 1/2 must give **more** than 1/2. She added the numerators and the denominators. Correct: 5/10 + 2/10 = **7/10**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Adding or subtracting the denominators: 1/3 + 1/4 ≠ 2/7.
Changing the denominator but not the numerator: 2/3 is 4/6, not 2/6.
Adding the denominators after making them equal: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6, not 5/12.
Not simplifying: 3/6 should be written as 1/2 when the question asks for simplest form.
In "what fraction is left?" questions, stopping before subtracting from 1.
Not checking with an estimate — an answer smaller than one of the fractions you added must be wrong.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Work out 3/4 − 1/6" with an answer box. On Paper 1 (no calculator) you must show the equivalent fractions.
"Give your answer in its simplest form" or "as a mixed number" — follow the instruction for the mark.
Missing-number problems: 1/2 + ☐/10 = 9/10.
Estimation: "Ring the best estimate" or "Is the answer more or less than 1? Explain."
Two-step word problems (eaten, spent, read … what is left?). Write the first step clearly for a method mark.
"Explain the mistake" questions — use an estimate ("the answer must be more than 1/2") or show the correct method.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Adding and subtracting fractions — practice
blocks.intro: 14 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. No calculator. Type fractions like 7/12 and mixed numbers like 1 3/4. For the explain question, mark yourself with the mark scheme.

questions.e: 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12. 2/7 adds the tops and bottoms (wrong); 2/12 and 1/7 are smaller than 1/3, so they cannot be right.

questions.q: Work out 3/5 + 1/2. Write your answer as a mixed number or an improper fraction.
Which is closest to the answer of 7/8 + 5/6?
questions.e: 7/8 is close to 1 and 5/6 is close to 1, so the answer is close to 2. (Exact: 21/24 + 20/24 = 41/24 = 1 17/24.)

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 11/12 − 1/10?
questions.e: 11/12 is close to 1 and 1/10 is close to 0, so the answer is about 1 − 0 = 1. (Exact: 55/60 − 6/60 = 49/60.)

questions.q: Which pair of fractions adds up to exactly 1?
Omar eats 1/3 of a cake. His sister eats 1/4 of the same cake. What fraction of the cake is left?

questions.e: Use eighths: 6/8 + 5/8 − 4/8 = 7/8. (1 mark for all three fractions correctly written as eighths, or for 11/8 seen.)

questions.q: Work out 2 1/2 − 3/4. Write your answer as a mixed number.
Without working out the exact answer, explain why 4/9 + 3/7 is less than 1.
questions.ms: 1 mark: both fractions are less than 1/2 (e.g. 4/9 < 4.5/9 = 1/2 and 3/7 < 3.5/7 = 1/2), so their sum is less than 1/2 + 1/2 = 1. Do not accept an exact calculation alone (55/63) — the question says without working out the exact answer.
questions.e: Half of 9 is 4.5, so 4/9 is less than 1/2. Half of 7 is 3.5, so 3/7 is less than 1/2. Two numbers each less than 1/2 add up to less than 1.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Estimate first: is each fraction close to 0, 1/2 or 1?
Make the denominators the same (use the lowest common multiple), using equivalent fractions.
Add or subtract the numerators only — the denominator stays the same.
Simplify, and change improper fractions to mixed numbers when asked.
"What is left?" → subtract from 1 whole (12/12, 8/8 …).
